subject: Critical Thinking
title: The Loaded Question: Trapped Before You Answer
description: One-minute skill: The Loaded Question: Trapped Before You Answer.

hook.text: 'Have you stopped cheating on exams?' Whether you answer yes or no, you've admitted to cheating.

buildup.text: A loaded question contains a hidden assumption. Answering it accepts the assumption, even if it's false.

discovery.text: Lawyers, journalists, and debaters use loaded questions to corner opponents into admissions they didn't intend.

twist.text: The correct response isn't yes or no — it's rejecting the premise: 'I reject the assumption in your question.'

climax.text: Most survey questions are subtly loaded. 'Do you support the wasteful government spending plan?' presumes it's wasteful.

punchline.text: Before answering a question, check what answering it admits.

quiz.question: What makes a question 'loaded'?
options: It contains a hidden assumption that any answer would accept

details.summary: A loaded question embeds a controversial assumption that any direct answer appears to confirm. 'Have you stopped cheating on tests?' presupposes cheating occurred, trapping the respondent regardless of their answer.
details.whyItMatters: Loaded questions appear in debates, interviews, and surveys. Recognizing them prevents you from accepting hidden premises you never agreed to.
takeaways: Any direct answer seems to confirm the assumption
The correct response is to challenge the premise explicitly

faq.question: How should you respond to a loaded question in a debate?
faq.answer: Reject the question's framing and address the hidden assumption directly. Say 'your question assumes X, which I do not accept.' This exposes the trap to the audience and resets the discussion to a fair starting point.

faq.question: How are loaded questions used in surveys to manipulate results?
faq.answer: Surveys can embed assumptions: 'How concerned are you about the government's reckless spending?' assumes spending is reckless. Respondents who answer the concern scale implicitly validate the characterization built into the question.
